_description: Part 13 - GA4/GTM-compatible event contract, CONTRACT ONLY, no implementation (this repo has zero existing GA4/GTM code - verified: no gtag/dataLayer/googletagmanager.com reference anywhere in src/, no NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID or similar env var, the only 'GA4' mention in the whole codebase is a plain-text line on the Stack page listing it as a tool the site owner uses professionally elsewhere, not a site-wide analytics install - so there is no existing convention here to match beyond the standard GA4 event-naming shape itself, which is what these names/parameters follow).

events.name: site_search_open
events.when: the search surface becomes visible/focused (whatever its eventual form - modal open, command-palette invoke, /search page load with focus) - fires once per open, not per keystroke.

events.name: site_search
events.when: a query is actually executed against the index (debounced - NOT one event per keystroke; fires once the user's typing settles or they explicitly submit).

parameters.search_term: see privacyEvaluation below - NOT sent raw, see recommendation
parameters.result_count: integer, search(query).results.length before any facet filtering
parameters.search_type: one of the 6 empty-state names in search-empty-states-contract.json, OR 'results' - lets analysis distinguish a broad-but-successful query from a genuinely-empty one without a second event

events.name: site_search_result_click
events.when: a result is actually opened/navigated to.

parameters.selected_result_id: the document's own search id (e.g. 'calculator:cac') - a stable, real, already-public identifier, not PII
parameters.selected_position: 1-indexed rank in the list the user saw at click time (post-balancing, post any active filters)
parameters.result_mode: 'ranked' or 'grouped' - which of search-result-modes-contract.json's two projections was on screen, so click-through-rate analysis isn't confounded by presentation

events.name: site_search_filter
events.when: a facet value is selected OR deselected (both directions, so filter abandonment is visible - not just filter application).

parameters.filter_type: the facet dimension (e.g. 'normalizedCategory', 'type') - one of the 9 named in search-facet-combination-contract.json
parameters.filter_value: the specific value selected/deselected (a real, controlled-vocabulary string from search-facets.json - not free text)

events.name: site_search_no_results
events.when: search settles into the noResults or filteredNoResults state from search-empty-states-contract.json - a dedicated event (not just inferable from site_search's result_count=0) because 0-result queries are a specific, high-value signal for finding corpus/synonym/alias gaps.

parameters.search_term: see privacyEvaluation - same treatment as site_search
parameters.had_active_filters: boolean - distinguishes noResults from filteredNoResults without a second event name

events.name: site_search_close
events.when: the search surface is dismissed without a result click - the natural complement to site_search_open, letting search-funnel drop-off be measured (open -> search -> [no click] -> close).

parameters.had_query: boolean - closed with an empty query (browsed away) vs. closed after typing something (didn't find what they wanted)

explicitlyNotAdded._description: Kept to exactly the 6 events named in the task brief plus their listed parameters, per the brief's own 'avoid event proliferation' instruction - candidates considered and deliberately NOT added:
rejected: site_search_scroll (scrolling further into results) - a lower-value signal than the 6 above; can be approximated later from result_count vs. selected_position if ever needed, without a new event.
site_search_typing (per-keystroke) - explicitly the wrong grain; site_search already debounces to one event per settled query.

site_search_group_toggle (switching ranked<->grouped mode, if that ever becomes a user-facing toggle) - real, but speculative until a design actually offers that toggle; add it then, not preemptively.

privacyEvaluation.risk: search_term (the raw query string) is free text a user typed - it CAN contain PII if someone searches for e.g. their own name, email, or another person's details, even though nothing in this corpus's own content is personal (it's all calculator/ab-test/journey/blog content). GA4 itself explicitly prohibits sending PII in any parameter (documented in Google's own GA4 terms) - sending raw search_term verbatim on every query is a real, avoidable compliance risk, not a theoretical one, since GA4 has no way to know a given query happens to contain a name someone typed by habit.
privacyEvaluation.recommendation: Send the NORMALIZED query (query-normalization-contract.json's own normalize()/tokenize() pipeline output - lowercased, diacritic-folded, punctuation-stripped, whitespace-collapsed) instead of the raw typed string, for BOTH site_search and site_search_no_results. This preserves 100% of the analytical value this contract's stated purpose needs (finding real corpus/synonym gaps, e.g. seeing 'donusum orani' show up as a frequent 0-result query) while removing the specific things that make free text risky: exact capitalization/spacing a person might've typed identifiably, and it's the SAME string the ranking system itself already computes and discards, so this requires no new logic, just reusing an existing pipeline output as the parameter value instead of req.query verbatim.
privacyEvaluation.residualRisk: Normalization does not remove PII that happens to BE the entire query content (e.g. someone types a full name - normalizing 'John Smith' still yields 'john smith', still a name). This is a smaller, harder-to-eliminate-in-software risk common to any query-logging system (Google Search Console, site-search-analytics tools generally accept it) - mitigated by NOT sending selected_result_id alongside a name-like query in a way that would let anyone reconstruct 'person X was interested in topic Y' (this corpus has no personal-data topics to leak, so the practical exposure here is low, but the parameter-level recommendation above is the concrete, implementable mitigation this contract commits to).

piiConfirmation: No parameter in the 6 events above carries a user identifier, IP, email, or any field that isn't either (a) the normalized query text (see privacyEvaluation) or (b) a real, publicly-visible corpus fact (result type/id/position, filter dimension/value) that is not personal data about the searcher.
